# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Fall of Jerusalem — God's Just Discipline

---

**8:1** Trouble and anguish crashed over me
more than over any people on earth.

**8:2** Jerusalem heard it and shook with anguish;
her daughters cried out in distress across the land.

**8:3** I put on sackcloth;
I threw my prayer like a cry toward the LORD:

**8:4** 'What have you done to us, O God?
What sin have we committed, that you bring this punishment down on us?'

**8:5** You laid our sins as a weight on our necks;
you stripped us bare for all our afflictions.

**8:6** The sons of Israel were scattered across the land of strangers —
not one redeemer to be found.

**8:7** For you drove them out in your anger;

**8:8** for the land was saturated with lawless deeds, with murders, with treachery;
those who did evil had multiplied beyond counting.

**8:9** The LORD saw all of it —
and hid his face, refusing to show pity.

**8:10** Not one man, not one woman, not one child, not a single descendant
escaped from the LORD's terrible punishment.

**8:11** The sky held its rain back from them;
the springs of the deep were sealed shut.

**8:12** There were no mountains high enough to shelter them,
no hills to give them any refuge.

**8:13** Their roads were more desolate than the desert tracks of the east;
those who walked them stumbled as if in blindness.

**8:14** Their sons and daughters went into grinding captivity —
necks stamped with the seal of slavery.

**8:15** God repaid them according to their own deeds;
he handed them over for the sins they had done.

**8:16** For God surrendered them to all the surrounding nations
to be shamed and spat upon.

**8:17** He had once chosen them from all the nations —
now he rejected them in his burning anger.

**8:18** For God alone is their redeemer;
he is the king of all the earth, the judge who is just.

**8:19** And so God turned me over — according to my heart's own desire — to the man from the east;
and I bore the yoke of his slavery.

**8:20** I watched him march on Jerusalem with the armies of the nations;
his face was terrible to behold.

**8:21** He seized the strong towers and the walls of Jerusalem —
and God let it happen.

**8:22** The ruler of the nations came up to Jerusalem
and placed his foot on her neck.

**8:23** He did not spare her beautiful young men;
he slaughtered them with the sword.

**8:24** He drove Jerusalem's leaders beyond the borders of the land
and sent the young men off to the distant sea.

**8:25** He turned the daughter of Jerusalem into a mockery for the nations;
her sons and daughters dragged away in wretched captivity.

**8:26** Because the sons of Israel had desecrated the LORD's holy things;
they had fouled the offerings of God with their lawless hands.

**8:27** He turned God's own altar into a stone to be trampled on;
all the glory of Jerusalem he converted to shame.

**8:28** He exposed Jerusalem's sins before all the nations;
her beauty was spread as plunder for every people under heaven.

**8:29** He laid her sins bare under the open sun —
and all the earth witnessed God's judgment executed in righteousness.

**8:30** Hidden away are God's judgments in the far corners of the earth;
who can understand God's justice except the one who fears him with full knowledge?

**8:31** Whoever understands these things will vindicate the LORD in his judgments —
for he is righteous; and those who do not understand will hold their peace.

**8:32** For the mercy of the LORD rests upon those who fear him,
through which he distinguishes in judgment between the righteous and the sinner.

**8:33** Blessed is the LORD, who judges all the earth in his righteousness.

**8:34** Israel, sing praise to the LORD by God's mercy;
let us bless the name of the LORD forever and ever!

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering prioritizing poetic force and contemporary resonance.*
